transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: After your surgery, it's generally okay to start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, please make sure to wear protective eyewear to avoid any risk of injury to your eyes.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. Next, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using the preservative-free eye drops for dryness four times a day as soon as you get home from the hospital. It's usually best to start with a gentle regimen like that and adjust as needed. If you're running low, your GP should be able to provide more.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. I'm also wondering, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. But if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to take a closer look.
transcript.delivered: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for your help. I don't have any more questions right now.
